submitter: bugfix_302_design_repair_verification lane, acting on bugs_open/317 (owner decision 3, 2026-08-19)
rationale:
The scheduled sweep 'claimed-item-timeout' (ENABLED, every 120s) auto-completes an item that has been 'claimed' past its timeout by writing site_work_items DIRECTLY. It does not call CompleteWorkItemAction, so NEITHER completion gate runs — not gate 2 (the verifier registry) and not gate 1b (noChangeGates). Its only protection is an item_type exclusion list, and migration 220's own comment states the contract it was written to: 'The item_type exclusion is the LOCKSTEP TWIN of the RegisterVerifier() calls'.

That contract was COMPLETE when gate 2 was the only gate. Gate 1b shipped 2026-08-13 (WII-017) with its own opt-in roster, and a type carrying a gate-1b roster entry but no registered verifier was therefore never excluded. dark_section_audit is exactly that type, and the only one today: it has a noChangeGates entry (and since bugs_closed/302 an unreadableRefuses declaration) and has no verifier deliberately — verifier_coverage_test.go classifies its family as needing a browser on the completion path, the standing objection this estate has refused three times. So for that type the sweep was a completion path no gate could see.

WHY THE GUARD MOVED PACKAGE, which is the substance of this change rather than an incidental. TestRegisteredVerifiersMatchClaimTimeoutExclusion could not be widened where it stood: it lives in discovery_checks, and noChangeGates lives in actions, which IMPORTS discovery_checks — so the second roster is unreadable from there at any cost. The replacement lives in actions, reads BOTH rosters live from the code that enforces them, and reads the exclusion list from the migration file. Neither half is a third copy that can drift. The old site keeps a comment saying where the guard went and why, so the next reader does not conclude it was deleted.

MEASURED, and filed as LATENT rather than as damage: archive-inclusive, 0 of 30 dark_section_audit and 0 of 498 hardcoded_section_colors completions carry the sweep's completed_by_step shape. It has never fired. The reason is contingent, not structural — both carriers that dispatch this type are enabled=false, so nothing claims these items and nothing times out. The owner ruled on 2026-08-19 to keep the carriers off for now AND to fix this, in that combination, precisely because re-enabling a carrier re-arms it.

SCOPE: council gate, not an RFC. Per the 2026-07-29 ruling 1, an RFC is owed when the shared mechanism's GUARANTEE changes. The guarantee here is unchanged in kind — 'the sweep must not complete an item a gate could have blocked' — and this change makes the implementation match the guarantee it already claimed, for one item_type. Nothing that was excluded becomes included; one type that should always have been excluded now is. Per the 2026-08-02 RFC_010 narrowing, no new authority ships: the exclusion list is a refusal list, and widening a refusal is the safe direction. The reverse direction of the guard is unchanged and still enforced.

WHAT COULD GO WRONG, stated rather than left for the reviewer: an over-wide exclusion list is not free — an excluded type that no gate can grade would fall through to the timeout reset for ever, which is the churn bugs_open/006 §C was filed about. That is why the guard keeps BOTH directions and why the union is asserted to be non-empty on each side separately: if noChangeGates were ever emptied, the union would silently collapse back to the gate-2-only contract this change exists to widen, and the guard fails loudly instead (mutation-proven).

plan.summary: Widen the claimed-item-timeout exclusion contract from 'has a registered verifier' to 'has a registered verifier OR a noChangeGates entry', apply it to the live scheduled_tasks.pre_query via a guarded migration, and move the parity guard to the one package that can read both rosters.

edits.rationale: Owning pipeline: the work-item dispatch/completion path (site-work-orchestrator and the dispatch loops), whose completions this sweep short-circuits. Adds dark_section_audit to the exclusion list on the LIVE column. Guarded as a DO block rather than a bare UPDATE: a read-before-write anchor aborts if the predicate has moved since this was written, an idempotence check aborts on a second application rather than appending a duplicate, and the post-write verification RAISEs — because ON_ERROR_STOP ignores a non-empty result set, so a verification block built from SELECTs cannot stop the COMMIT. 220 is deliberately NOT edited: it is applied history and editing it would make its recorded checksum a lie.
Removes the added type and verifies the removal by RAISE. Its own comment states the cost of using it: applying the rollback re-opens bugs_open/317.
edits.sketch:
+UPDATE scheduled_tasks SET pre_query = replace(pre_query, ', dark_section_audit', '') ...
+IF n <> 0 THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'ABORT: rollback did not remove it'; END IF;

edits.rationale: The widened guard, in the only package that can see both rosters. Asserts the contract in BOTH directions over the union, and asserts each roster is non-empty SEPARATELY so a failure names which one went missing — without that, emptying noChangeGates would silently narrow the guard back to the gate-2-only contract this change exists to widen. Reads the NEWEST matching migration, because 220 stays as history and a later migration owns the live predicate.

Superseded, and it had to be removed rather than left: once the exclusion list carries a type with no registered verifier, its reverse direction fails by design. Proven to fail before deletion rather than assumed. A comment is left in its place explaining where the guard went and the import-direction reason it could not stay, so a reader does not conclude the estate simply dropped a guard.
edits.sketch:
-func TestRegisteredVerifiersMatchClaimTimeoutExclusion(t *testing.T) { ... }
+// The claimed-item-timeout lockstep guard USED TO LIVE HERE. It moved 2026-08-19 to ... because noChangeGates lives in `actions`, which imports this package.

edits.rationale: Registers the widened seam in the same commit that ships it, per the 2026-07-28 ordering exemption condition (2). Records the package-move reason, the newest-migration rule, the latency measurement, the mutation matrix, and the authoring trap (a migration in this family must not spell the exclusion clause in prose above its real declaration — the regex takes the first occurrence, and this migration's own comment tripped it).
edits.sketch: +### WII-019 — The claim-timeout exclusion is the lockstep twin of BOTH completion gates, not just the verifier registry

grounded_in: Migration 220's own comment, which states the contract being widened: 'The item_type exclusion is the LOCKSTEP TWIN of the RegisterVerifier() calls in platform/orchestration/actions/discovery_checks/: those item types have a Go verifier that…'

MEASURED 2026-08-19, the live predicate BEFORE: 13 item types, exactly matching the 13 RegisterVerifier/RegisterVerifierWithPolicy call sites — so the gate-2 lockstep was intact and the gap was specifically gate 1b.

MEASURED 2026-08-19, archive-inclusive (site_work_items UNION site_work_items_archive, because the live table is a ~7-day window): 0 of 30 dark_section_audit and 0 of 498 hardcoded_section_colors completions carry the sweep's completed_by_step shape. Never fired.

MEASURED 2026-08-19: scheduled_tasks 'claimed-item-timeout' enabled=true interval_seconds=120; 'improvement-sweep' enabled=false; 'site-discovery-rotation-design' enabled=false. The sweep runs constantly; it is the CLAIMING that is absent, which is why this is latent rather than structural.

VERIFIED at the live column after applying: the exclusion list holds 14 item types and its set is IDENTICAL to the one parsed out of the declared migration file; dark_section_audit appears exactly once; a second application ABORTS with 'this migration has been applied'.

Mutation matrix, exit-status gated with an unmutated control and both files restored byte-identical (diff -q): drop the type from the list -> RED ('has a noChangeGates entry (gate 1b) but is NOT excluded'); add a type no gate can grade -> RED ('NO gate can grade it'); empty noChangeGates -> RED ('gate 1b is inert').

The import direction that forced the package move: platform/orchestration/actions imports platform/orchestration/actions/discovery_checks (verified in complete_work_item_verification.go's import block), so a test in discovery_checks cannot read noChangeGates at any cost.

bugs_open/006 §C is why the reverse direction must stay: the sweep's generic branch exists because 15 of 18 types had no evidence test and were re-running finished work, so an over-wide exclusion list reintroduces that churn.
